current_question.prompt: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers that add up to target.
current_question.carl_focus: Explain approach, complexity, and edge cases cleanly.

recent_turns.text: Walk me through how you'd start on Two Sum.
I can check every pair with two nested loops, which is O(n^2), and I'm not sure how to make it faster.

reference_response: Your nested-loop baseline is a clean starting point! Ask yourself what repeated work the inner loop is doing on every step, and what extra memory could let you check whether the needed partner value has already been seen.

current_question.prompt: Implement TTLLRUCache(capacity) with O(1) average get and put, evicting expired keys before live keys when at capacity.
current_question.carl_focus: Data structures, invariants, and edge cases.

recent_turns.text: How are you thinking about tracking both recency and expiration?
I'm stuck because updating recency needs one order, while expiration times can be in a completely different order.

reference_response: Spotting that recency and expiration follow two different orders is the exact right insight! Try separating how you handle an expired key when it's read versus when you actually need to free a slot at capacity.

current_question.prompt: Design a multi-channel notification service (push, email, SMS) with rate limiting and user preferences.
core_requirements: Retry with backoff for flaky providers

recent_turns.text: Where would you like to begin?
There are so many moving parts—queues, providers, templates—I'm not sure what to draw first.

reference_response: Start simple—sketch just one notification's happy path from the triggering service through an API and preference check to a delivery worker. Once that core spine is on the board, layering in retries and deduplication becomes much easier.

current_question.prompt: Design a multi-region double-entry payments ledger handling 50k TPS.

recent_turns.text: An airline merchant hits 8,000 TPS into one settlement account row—how do you avoid write lock contention?
I'm thinking about adding read replicas, though I know writes still hit the same single row.

workspace_context.diagram_summary: Merchant SDK -> API Gateway -> Ledger API -> Spanner Ledger DB

reference_response: You already spotted the core constraint—replicas won't relieve single-row write contention. Think about how you could spread concurrent writes for one busy merchant across multiple independent rows and reconcile them when reading the total.

current_question.prompt: Tell me about a time you drove cross-team alignment when partner teams had competing priorities.
current_question.carl_focus: Show empathy for partner constraints, personal leverage, measurable outcome, and Learning.

recent_turns.text: Tell me about a time you drove cross-team alignment.
Three product teams didn't want to adopt our shared auth SDK because their Q3 roadmaps were full, so I met with each lead and built a lightweight adapter to make migration easy.

reference_response: Building that lightweight adapter is a great Action—now land the story with what actually changed afterward (adoption, time saved, or incidents avoided) and one short lesson you'd reuse on your next cross-team rollout.

current_question.prompt: Describe an ambiguous 0-to-1 technical initiative you owned.
current_question.carl_focus: Clarify personal technical framing, key tradeoffs, and org-level impact.

Our team noticed search latency was climbing so we researched a few engines, built a prototype, and rolled out a new indexing pipeline.

reference_response: You have a crisp setup on the search latency problem—now zoom into one pivotal decision or tradeoff you personally made while evaluating engines, and close with the measurable outcome.

current_question.prompt: Implement an incremental SSEParser with feed(chunk) handling arbitrary chunk boundaries and CRLF.
current_question.carl_focus: Streaming edge cases and clean invariants.

recent_turns.text: Your second test is failing on the CRLF chunk—want a quick nudge?
Yes please, it works when the whole string is in one chunk but breaks when split across two calls.

reference_response: You're very close since single-chunk input already passes! Trace what happens to your parser state when a two-character line ending gets cut right in half between the end of one chunk and the start of the next.

current_question.prompt: Walk me through a meaningful technical mistake or incident you owned.
current_question.carl_focus: Honest ownership, swift mitigation, and systemic prevention.

recent_turns.text: What mistake comes to mind?
I'm worried about sounding bad if I pick a real prod outage I caused.

reference_response: Picking a real mistake actually builds strong Senior trust—interviewers care far less about perfection than how calmly you recovered. Keep the mistake summary brief, then spend most of your time on the permanent guardrail you built afterward.

current_question.prompt: Return parallel topological execution waves for tasks and prerequisite deps; throw Error if a cycle exists.
current_question.carl_focus: Graph invariants, wave grouping, duplicate edges.

recent_turns.text: How are you thinking about grouping tasks into parallel waves?
I can tell which tasks have no prerequisites at the start, but I'm unsure how to detect a cycle cleanly.

reference_response: Starting from tasks with zero prerequisites is a great anchor! Once you run a wave and unlock newly ready tasks, think about what it means for the total number of scheduled tasks if a cycle is hiding in the graph.

current_question.prompt: Design a globally distributed API rate limiter with <5ms hot-path latency.
core_requirements: Graceful degradation if state store fails

recent_turns.text: How do you enforce a global per-minute limit across us-east and eu-west without paying cross-region RTT on every request?
If every gateway calls a central US store, EU latency jumps by 90ms, so I'm stuck on how to stay accurate and fast.

workspace_context.diagram_summary: EU Gateway -> Central US Store; US Gateway -> Central US Store

reference_response: Naming that 90ms cross-region RTT bottleneck is spot-on! Ask yourself what happens if each region makes fast local decisions and syncs counts asynchronously—and what small accuracy tradeoff you'd accept in exchange.

current_question.prompt: Tell me about a time you pushed back on an aggressive product deadline due to reliability concerns.
current_question.carl_focus: Frame risk in business terms and offer constructive options.

recent_turns.text: Walk me through a time you pushed back on a deadline.
I told the PM our database wasn't ready for the promo launch and we needed two more weeks, and they got frustrated.

reference_response: You clearly owned the reliability risk—next, highlight how you translated that database risk into customer or revenue impact and whether you offered a phased alternative instead of a flat delay.

current_question.prompt: Given busy intervals for multiple attendees, a day window, and duration, return all merged free slots of length >= duration.

recent_turns.text: How would you simplify handling multiple attendees' calendars at once?
Comparing every attendee's schedule against every other attendee feels really messy.

reference_response: Great instinct avoiding pairwise attendee comparisons! Think about whether it matters *who* is busy during a slot—if you view all busy blocks as one combined timeline, how do the free gaps jump out?
